start.promptSummary: Near-vertical true-colour fictional Korean-style river-estuary-sea satellite mosaic with two aligned adjacent tiles and one subtle acquisition-tone seam; no derived field yet
start.qa: Original size reviewed: one connected estuary from upper-right river to left-side sea, continuous coastline and roads, plausible regional-scale fields and settlement, visible central acquisition seam without geographic break, no labels or spacecraft.

end.promptSummary: Edit selected start image, preserve the same geography, resolve the acquisition seam and introduce a muted water-only qualitative environmental field from river mouth seaward
end.qa: Original size reviewed: tile seam resolves, muted teal field follows the connected river and nearshore water, no evident dry-land spill, labels, scan beam or dashboard. The end image is one pixel narrower, so normalize image dimensions during video input preflight without altering source originals.

registrationAudit.method: OpenCV ORB feature matches on downloaded originals, partial affine RANSAC threshold 3 px
registrationAudit.assessment: Same geographic frame is well registered at feature scale; image generation may still alter local pixels. Review exact shore and sandbar boundaries in video frames.

storyboard.camera: Fixed near-vertical orthographic view; no pan, zoom or rotation required
storyboard.start0s: Two aligned true-colour raster tiles show one subtle tonal acquisition seam across continuous land and water; no water-condition field yet
storyboard.phase0to2s: The tile boundary remains in geographic coordinates while the two registered tiles balance and join; the seam and tone offset disappear while roads, fields, coast and river stay fixed
storyboard.phase2to4s: A blue-to-teal water-condition front becomes visible in the upper-right upstream river, travels continuously through the existing channel and reaches the mouth; the change is spatial movement, not opacity flashing or a full-frame crossfade
storyboard.phase4to6s: That connected front proceeds from the mouth into the adjacent coastal sea, spreads laterally into the accepted end-image footprint and softens at its outer edge; original photographic water texture stays visible
storyboard.end6s: One coherent regional mosaic and legible environmental layer, matching the supplied end image on the same geography
storyboard.transition: Cut from this regional water/data view to a distinct broad field-observation shot
rejectionConditions: Shoreline, sandbars, roads, fields or settlements move or morph
Environmental colour appears over dry land, exposed sand or vegetation
Seam merely blinks while no meaningful water-information layer resolves
The two images merely crossfade, or the field fades in everywhere at once rather than advancing upstream-to-mouth-to-sea
Model mesh, spacecraft, scan beam, text, numbers, fake interface or new terrain appear
Start/end frames do not correspond to their accepted downloaded originals

videoPlan.uploadAudit: Both original PNG files uploaded in one Higgsfield browser file chooser. CDN images were decoded and compared to local originals: start UUID mean RGB absolute pixel difference 0.56, end UUID 0.65 after same-size normalization; roles verified and not swapped.
videoPlan.prompt: Use the uploaded START IMAGE as the first frame and the uploaded END IMAGE as the last frame of one continuous six-second 16:9 scientific editorial video. Both images show the SAME fictional regional satellite mosaic, with one connected river, estuary, tidal flats, coast, fields, roads and settlement. Keep this entire geography in fixed near-vertical registration throughout. The camera is completely locked: no zoom, pan, tilt, rotation, crop change or perspective change. At 0 seconds show the original two aligned true-colour satellite tiles with their subtle vertical acquisition-tone seam and no derived water-condition field. From 0 to 2 seconds, the tile boundary remains at the exact same geographic coordinate while the two tiles progressively balance and join into one seamless true-colour mosaic; every shoreline, channel, sandbar, road and field stays fixed. From 2 to 4 seconds, a restrained muted blue-to-teal qualitative environmental layer begins in the existing upper-right upstream river water. Its visible leading edge travels continuously down the existing channel through the bends and reaches the mouth. From 4 to 6 seconds, that same connected water-only front spreads from the mouth into the adjacent open sea, widens laterally and softens at its outer edge until it matches the supplied END IMAGE. The action must be a legible advancing and changing spatial data field, not a full-frame crossfade, opacity pulse, instant all-at-once tint or camera movement. Preserve the true-colour image texture beneath the translucent layer. Keep every coloured pixel strictly inside connected wet water and off dry tidal flats, marsh vegetation, roads, fields and land. No new islands, channels, roads, buildings, clouds, model mesh, arrows, labels, numbers, legend, dashboard, scan beam, spacecraft, text, logo or decorative particles. This is an accelerated explanatory satellite-data processing concept, not a measured result, actual site or real-time physical transport. Silent.
